title: mx self-update: a real upgrade path for the mx client (release channel + updater + notifier + distribution)
description:
**Goal.** `mx` knows when it is out of date, says so once a day without being asked, and upgrades itself with one command on every install kind we support (release tarball, Homebrew, source checkout, bare copied binary), verifying what it downloads and never leaving a half-installed state. Rollback is one command.

**Why.** Today's `mx self-update` is a dev-only rebuild-from-checkout (needs cargo, a checkout, sudo) with a broken marker-file fallback (gjl). The release workflow has never run, there are no tags or releases, `scripts/package.sh` is untracked (d5c), Linux/draft-publish/Homebrew are TODO comments, and the tap repo is empty. Nothing in mx compares versions to anything.

**Spec.** docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-mx-self-update-design.md (branch feat/self-update, worktree .worktrees/self-update). Read it before any child task; the decisions below are the short form.

**Decisions already made (spec §3):**
- Channel: GitHub Releases on the public repo unyform-ai/mech-crate-releases; `releases/latest` is the source of truth; assets `mx-v<ver>-<triple>.tar.gz` + `.sha256` exactly as scripts/package.sh emits; `MX_RELEASES_API` overrides the base URL (the wiremock seam); GITHUB_TOKEN honored, never required.
- Layout: `~/.mech-crate/releases/mx-v<ver>/` = an extracted tarball (already a valid MechCrate root — `mech_crate_root()` walks up to `scripts/`); `~/.mech-crate/current` symlink is the only thing an update changes (rename-flip, atomic); shims in `~/.local/bin`; keep current + one previous for `--rollback`; no sudo anywhere in the release path.
- Engine: new `mx_lib::selfupdate` with pure core (version, target, kind, plan) and effectful shell (index, fetch, layout, verify); `flate2`+`tar` in-process extraction; sha256 mandatory; macOS `codesign --verify` when available; post-update refresh of templates, version file, and the mcp wrapper script.
- Command: `mx self-update [--check|--dry-run|--yes|--to <ver>|--rollback|--from-dir <dir>|--pull|--refresh-cache]`; `--check` exits 10 when an update exists. (`--version` is clap's global flag, hence `--to`.)
- Notifier: reads a 24h cache, spawns a detached `--refresh-cache` when stale, prints one stderr line only on a TTY; skipped for self-update/--version/--help/mcp run, and under CI / MX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 / config/update.toml check=false; offline backoff 1h.
- Homebrew kind delegates to `brew upgrade mx`; Source kind keeps today's rebuild flow and fixes gjl via `paths::recorded_source_root`.

**Phasing.** P1 = a working updater on macOS (package.sh committed, pipeline dry-run + first tag v0.1.2, lib module, command rewrite, gjl fix, cli-reference row). P2 = frictionless (notifier, Linux job, draft-then-publish, curl installer at mechcrate.dev/install.sh, docs). P3 = ecosystem (Homebrew formula + tap-bump job, doctor line).

**Execution model.** Library tasks are TDD in the worktree; each child lists acceptance criteria a memoryless worker can verify with `cargo nextest` / `assert_cmd`. Pipeline tasks record their evidence (run URLs, asset URLs) in the issue. One PR per phase from feat/self-update; a human merges; the P1 gate is a real `mx self-update` on this machine from a tagged release.

**Done when:** `mx self-update --check` reports the latest tag; `mx self-update` on a release install downloads, verifies, flips current, and `mx --version` reports the new version; `--rollback` restores the previous; the notifier hint appears once on a TTY and never in scripts; Linux and macOS tarballs publish from one tag through a draft; `curl mechcrate.dev/install.sh | sh` installs on a clean machine; known-broken gjl test passes; d5c and gjl closed.

**Known risks.** (1) Release secrets on Dev916/mech-crate are unverified (gh secret list returned nothing — may be a permission limit); the dry-run task settles it before any code depends on a tag. (2) A half-uploaded release must never be `latest` — draft-then-publish is P2 but the P1 dry run uses a single-asset release so the window is small. (3) Replacing the running binary: the symlink flip keeps the running inode; the Bare kind renames over the file in the same directory, which POSIX allows. (4) Corpus retrieval was lexical-only during design; guidance drawn was the house rules (atomic rename, idempotency, pure core/effectful shell, IO-boundary contract tests), cited per decision in the spec.
acceptance_criteria: See 'Done when' in the description; each child carries its own verifiable criteria.

title: mx-mcp retrieval is lexical-only (no embedding key in the MCP env) — fix before the wave gates
description:
**Finding (2026-09-01):** `mcp__mx__rag_search` answers with `> Note: lexical-only search (no embedding key configured); results may be weaker.` — every agent query through the MCP server is trigram-only, and lexical-only retrieval is known to be nearly inert here (see mech-crate-4jw). The retrieval smoke tests in the wave gates are meaningless until this is fixed.

**Root cause:** `crates/mx-lib/src/corpus/config.rs:87` takes the embedding key from `MX_RAG_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` env or `embedding_api_key` in `~/.mech-crate/config/rag.toml`. The MCP server is launched from `.mcp.json` (`/usr/local/bin/mx-mcp --mech-crate-root …`, env has only `MECH_CRATE_ROOT`), so none of those are set; the CLI path works only because `mx rag ingest` is run from a shell that sourced `.env.secrets`.

**Fix options**
- (a) RECOMMENDED: add `embedding_api_key = "…"` to `~/.mech-crate/config/rag.toml` (user-local, untracked; the file already holds the Neon DSN). Zero code change.
- (b) Teach `mx-mcp` to read `<mech-crate-root>/.env.secrets` when the key is unset (small Rust change; keeps one source of truth for the key).
- (c) Put `MX_RAG_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` in the user-level Claude MCP config (~/.claude.json) — NOT in the checked-in `.mcp.json`.

Whichever lands: add an `mx doctor` (or `rag_health`) warning "embedding key missing — lexical-only", and document the key source in `docs/development/mx-mcp~usage.md`. Verify by calling `mcp__mx__rag_search` after restarting the MCP server: the lexical-only note must be gone and semantic hits (e.g. "graceful shutdown" → rust-async-cancellation doc) must rank first.
acceptance_criteria:
- mcp__mx__rag_search no longer prints 'lexical-only search (no embedding key configured)'
- The fix does not put a secret into a tracked file (.mcp.json is checked in)
- docs/development/mx-mcp~usage.md documents where the MCP server gets its embedding key
notes: 2026-09-02 root cause: NOT just a missing key. Two layers: (1) the MCP env has no key AND the session server started before rag.toml had one — fixed by writing embedding_api_key into ~/.mech-crate/config/rag.toml (mode 600, done; config path + file precedence verified in corpus/config.rs). (2) With the key in place, embeddings still fail: OpenAI returns 429 insufficient_quota / credit_balance_exhausted — the account has no credits. Verified by direct /v1/embeddings probe (2 attempts). CONSEQUENCE: wave-gate 'mx rag ingest' cannot embed new profile chunks until either (a) credits are added at platform.openai.com (Mike-only, billing) or (b) embedding_base_url in rag.toml is repointed at a local OpenAI-compatible provider + 'mx rag ingest --reembed' of all 2148 chunks (retrieval-characteristics decision — Mike's call). Authoring is unblocked ('--dry-run' never embeds). Also shipped: 'mx rag status' now prints 'Embedding key: configured/MISSING', the MCP lexical-only note names all three causes, and mx-mcp~usage.md documents key resolution. bin/mx + bin/mx-mcp (tracked, stale since Jul 18) refreshed from the rebuilt release.

title: [bug] astro recipe compose: 'include: optional: true' is not a Compose field — make dev hard-fails without db/redis
description:
Found during the mechcrate.dev site dogfood pass (site/ is an astro-recipe mx project).

templates/recipes/astro/docker/compose/service.yml opens with:

    include:
      - path: ../../docker/compose/db.yml
        optional: true
      - path: ../../docker/compose/redis.yml
        optional: true

Compose's `include` long syntax accepts path / project_directory / env_file. There is NO `optional` field (that belongs to `env_file`). The key is silently ignored, so a missing db.yml is a hard error, not a skip.

Repro (measured 2026-08-25, Docker 29.4.0 / Compose 5.1.2):
  mx add site --recipe astro   # without also adding db + redis
  make dev
  => open <proj>/docker/compose/db.yml: no such file or directory
     make: *** [dev] Error 2

Any astro service scaffolded without db AND redis siblings cannot start at all. The service also carries depends_on: {db,redis}: condition: service_healthy, which would fail for the same reason even if include were fixed.

Scope: astro only. No other recipe has an include block (grep -rln 'optional: true' templates/recipes/*/docker/compose/ returns astro's service.yml alone).

Fix options: (a) drop include+depends_on and let db/redis be composed by the project, (b) make db/redis a recipe option that emits the include only when selected. The site's own workaround is (a) — see site/docker/compose/site.yml, which documents the deviation inline.

Note this bug is invisible to the installer round-trip conformance tests: they assert 'mx add' applies cleanly, not that the resulting project can 'make dev'.

title: Passive update notifier: 24h cache, detached refresh, one stderr line on a TTY, opt-outs
description: The 'frictionless' half (spec §3.6). In mx_lib::selfupdate add notify.rs: Cache { checked_at, next_check_at, latest, current_at_check } at ~/.mech-crate/cache/update-check.json; pure decide(cache, now, current, is_tty, env) -> Action { Silent, Spawn, Hint(latest) | SpawnAndHint }. In crates/mx-cli/src/main.rs after the command runs (before exit code propagation): skip entirely when the subcommand is self-update, mcp run, or when --version/--help handled by clap (they exit before main's match); skip when stderr is not a TTY, CI is set, MX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1, or ~/.mech-crate/config/update.toml has check = false; else read the cache; if older than 24h (or missing) spawn '<current_exe> self-update --refresh-cache' detached with stdin/stdout/stderr = null (std::process::Command + spawn, do not wait; on unix setsid via pre_exec or the process-group trick so it outlives the parent); if the cache says latest > current print exactly one stderr line: 'mx <latest> is available (you have <current>). Run: mx self-update' with 'brew upgrade mx' substituted for the Homebrew kind; suppress repeat prints within 24h by recording hinted_at/hinted_version in the cache. Implement --refresh-cache: call ReleaseIndex::latest() with a 5s timeout, write the cache; on failure write next_check_at = now + 1h and exit 0 silently. Foreground cost must be one small file read: no network, no waiting.

title: [bug] astro recipe compose: build target 'runner' matches no Dockerfile stage — make up/build fails
description:
Found during the mechcrate.dev site dogfood pass.

templates/recipes/astro/docker/compose/service.yml:20 declares:

    build:
      target: runner

templates/recipes/astro/docker/dockerfiles/app.Dockerfile defines stages: base, deps, builder, development, production. There is no 'runner' stage, so any non-dev path (make up, make build, make release) fails to resolve the build target.

Measured across all 7 recipes 2026-08-25 — astro is the only outlier:
  astro/service.yml         target: runner      <-- no such stage
  laravel/service.yml       target: production  ok
  nuxt/service.yml          target: production  ok
  rust-api/service.yml      target: production  ok
  rust-leptos/service.yml   target: production  ok
  rust-worker/service.yml   target: production  ok
  zola/service.yml          target: production  ok

Not hit by the site dogfood because make dev's override sets target: development, which does exist.

Likely fix: s/runner/production/ in the astro service.yml template. Worth checking at the same time whether the production stage's CMD ['node','./dist/server/entry.mjs'] is right for astro apps configured with static output — it is not, and mechcrate.dev is exactly such an app (it deploys as a static bundle to Cloudflare and never runs this container).

title: Recipe scaffolders never run: directories created before init_app trips skip_if_exists
description: RecipeInstaller creates the recipe's 'directories' list before running init_app, so for astro/nuxt/zola the skip_if_exists guard always trips and the app scaffolder (npm create astro / nuxi init / zola init) never actually executes. Found by the first-touch-killers fix agent (PR #28) while writing installer round-trip conformance tests; out of scope there. Fix: run init_app before creating directories, or narrow skip_if_exists to check for the app's own marker files instead of the directory.

title: make dev s="a b" multi-service selection not supported (unquoted expansion + single-service compose_context_files)
description: templates/make/dev.mk expands $(MAKE) _dev service=$(call get_service_optional) unquoted, so a space-separated s= value makes the second name a make goal ('No rule to make target'). Even quoted, templates/scripts/dev.sh passes a single positional and compose_context_files (templates/scripts/.bashrc:85) resolves exactly one docker/compose/${service}.yml. Feature gap vs the 'run only the subset' pitch: fix needs quoting in dev.mk plus a loop over a service list in compose_context_files. Found by README claim audit 2026-08-19; README now shows only single-service s=.

title: env_file order inverted in 8 recipe compose files: secrets->shared flips precedence
description: Documented order is .env.shared -> .env.secrets -> .env.<service> (last wins). 9 template compose files honor it, but 8 recipe files list secrets BEFORE shared (rust-api/rust-leptos/nuxt/astro service.yml; laravel service.yml, service.worker.yml, service.worker.dev.yml, service.scheduler.yml), so .env.shared silently wins key collisions there — inverted precedence vs docs and vs the other 9 files. Mechanical fix: reorder env_file lists to match the documented order. Found by README claim audit 2026-08-19; README softened 'always' until fixed.
notes: Site T7 measurement adds: zola recipe omits .env.secrets from env_file entirely (third variant of the ordering drift)

title: rust-api scaffold cannot make dev unaided — secrets/env interpolation gap
